title: Prototype stage
body:
decade is a Wayland compositor that runs inside a window, organised into
sessions and panes for agent workflows, with a channel between an agent
harness and the apps it drives.

The compositor part is standard. Any Wayland client is a pane, drawn into a
rectangle of the decade window, with keyboard and pointer forwarded to it. A
terminal is ghostty running as a client. A code viewer is an editor running
as a client. decade writes neither.

The decade part is the chrome around the panes, drawn as a grid of character
cells under the TUI rule, and a unix socket per decade-aware app carrying
structured messages in both directions, such as scroll to this function,
highlight these lines, or the user clicked here. A plain app shows and takes
input but has no agent channel.

An earlier plan had decade write its own terminal emulator and its own
pixel-region protocol. It was dropped on 2026-11-06 because a compositor gets
both from a protocol every app already speaks, and the agent channel, which is
the point of the project, is the same either way.

Nothing goes into the README or `CLAUDE.md` until something runs. This body
is the description until then. The code today is a wgpu window drawing a
cell grid with three empty panes and a status line.

## Pieces

| Issue | State |
|---|---|
| Pane primitive, decade-185686 | Closed. Wayland buffers for app panes, cells for chrome and native panes |
| Pane transport, decade-f51dcd | Closed. Wayland for drawing and input, a socket per decade-aware app for messages |
| Host renderer, decade-1c11b4 | Open again. smithay renders with GLES and imports client buffers through EGL; wgpu may not survive |
| Harness chat pane, decade-9e4347 | Open. A native stand-in first |
| Spike, decade-3079aa | Open. smithay's winit backend hosts ghostty in a pane |

## Out of scope

- A remote-machine protocol in herdr's shape. It gets its own milestone once
  the socket exists.
- XWayland. X11 apps come later through smithay's xwayland module.
- The socket message format. It gets its own issue once the spike shows an
  app in a pane.

## Open

- Whether decade runs under compositors other than Hyprland. As a Wayland
  client it should. Only a test says.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/618aab71
notes.text: Language question, raised 2026-11-06 and settled for now. decade stays in Rust on smithay. The alternative taken seriously is Zig on wlroots, as river does it. The trigger to revisit is one thing only: the spike decade-3079aa finds something the nested compositor needs that smithay's winit backend cannot do and wlroots' nested backend can. Everything outside the compositor core, which is the socket protocol, the harness, process management, the text pane and the tests, is better in Rust either way.
